description: §13.2 — two independent whole-result cell writes of server calls, `@a = one(1); @b = two(2)`, followed by a read of both. impl#1 runs the two calls concurrently (a Promise.all batch) and lands the writes in source order before the read, so #indep yields `indep:7,7` with the stub answering 7 for both fns. The observable contract pinned here is the SEQUENCING half (the read sees both writes); whether the calls overlap is timing, which this harness does not observe.
rationale: §13.2: "Independent server calls in the same function body SHALL be parallelized in generated code unless there is a data dependency between them" and dependent operations SHALL be sequenced with `await`. The read `@seen = … @a … @b` depends on both writes, so it must observe both resolved values whatever the scheduling of the two calls. S478 (bootstrap triage C12): SPEC §19.9.10 (S451/S454): "A call made on the client whose callee is server-placed is a **failable call** at that site, whether or not the callee is declared `!`. It SHALL be handled exactly as a call to a `!` function (§19.4.3) … An unhandled one SHALL be **E-ERROR-002**"; its failure set is "`f`'s declared variants plus ONE wrapper variant `Transport(t: ServerCallError)`; a non-`!` callee fails with `Transport` alone" (S454 F1). The handler now covers `.Transport`.
